heartbeat_prompt_under_test: Daemon.heartbeatPrompt (see Daemon.swift) — the reflective fallback used whenever the goals ledger is absent or empty, which as of this writing is always, for every site

rubric.no_boilerplate_intro: the reply's opening sentence(s) must not restate who Fin is or what it generically does — phrases like 'Hello! I'm Fin, your terminal agent' / 'I'm ready to help you with your tasks' / 'I'll be driving the terminal work, keeping you updated' are all instances of the same forbidden pattern, regardless of exact wording
rubric.no_passive_handback_when_inferable: the reply must not end by asking the user what to do next (e.g. 'What would you like me to do?', 'What's our first mission?', 'Just let me know') when the immediately preceding turns already established a concrete pending action to check on or continue
rubric.reports_or_acts_on_real_state: the reply must state what actually changed or was learned since the last turn, or take a concrete next action with a tool — not a generic offer of future help

Checking whether it's proposed a fix or needs one from me — will update you once it responds, or sooner if it needs a decision only you can make.

scenarios.note_on_expected: no_passive_handback and reports_real_state are not scored as failures here specifically — with nothing pending, there is nothing to infer or report, and there is a real difference between 'no directive has arrived yet' (fine to stay quiet) and 'a directive is pending a reply' (hc01). Only the repeated self-introduction is unconditionally wrong.
